messages:
linus: Heads-up — saw a customer hit primary model saturation and the router auto-fell back to a compatible variant. Cost went up ~2.5x for that tenant and a couple of prompts regressed. Notified CS.

tanya: which customer + tier? logs/trace id?

linus: tenant=acme-inc (enterprise), tier=dedicated, trace=trace/20240412/xyz. Saturation window 14:03-14:07 UTC. Router decision: fallback_on_capacity = true for that model group.

cassie: hmm enterprise should prefer local fallback variants before spilling to shared hosts. Is tenant-aware routing skipping that? :thinking_face:

miguel: attaching snippet of the current router policy we ship:

```json
{"routing": {"priority": ["primary","compatible_variant"], "fallback_on_capacity": true, "max_variant_latency_ms": 250, "tenant_tier_rules": {"enterprise": "prefer_local", "standard": "spill_to_shared"}}}
```

linus: that policy is what we shipped but the runtime matched the compatible variant in a different region (eu-west) because local pool was saturated and regional fallback was allowed. For enterprise we promised region affinity — console config said "prefer_local", but the routing decision used cost-priority.

tanya: so two problems: console UX/confusion (shows prefer_local) and routing precedence mismatch (cost vs tier). Also we need telemetry to show when fallback ignored prefer_local.

miguel: agree. propose change: explicit precedence matrix: tenant_tier_rules > region_affinity > cost. Also emit metric: router.fallback.reason => {capacity, cost, latency, quota}. Add tag tenant_tier.

cassie: +1. Also add a transparent header for callers so customers can detect variant: `X-Redwood-Model-Variant: phoenix-v2-quant`. Avoid silent reroutes for enterprise without opt-in.

linus: API debate: some teams want silent fallback for SLA preservation, others want explicit failure to avoid cost surprises. We should support both with a per-tenant flag: auto_fallback = (true|false|notify_only).

tanya: console UX: add a per-tenant toggle (policy level) with three states and a tooltip enumerating tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs accuracy). Show historical fallback heatmap and cost delta preview for last 30 days.

miguel: telemetry fields to add: `fallback.count`, `fallback.latency_delta_ms`, `fallback.cost_delta_usd_per_1000`, `fallback.regression_rate_by_eval_set`. Link them under rollout -> incidents panel.

sre-bot: Incident alert: router.fallback.capacity spike for model: phoenix-v3 at 2024-04-12T14:03Z — 38 fallbacks in 4m. Autoremediation: triggered burst from dedicated pool.

linus: action items: 1) change precedence in router (miguel) 2) add router.fallback.reason tag & metrics (tanya) 3) console toggle + heatmap (cassie) 4) add response header and opt-in policy (linus). Estimated 1-2 sprints depending on infra churn.

cassie: UX notes: default for enterprise should be "notify_only" not silent auto_fallback. Provide rollout wizard to switch to silent after testing. Add audit log entry when fallback occurs.

miguel: quick config sketch (proposal):

```yaml
tenant_policies:
  acme-inc:
    auto_fallback: notify_only
    prefer_local: true
    allowed_regions: [us-west, us-east]
    fallback_variants: [quantized-compat, latency-optimized]
```

linus: last thought — we need a cheap guardrail: ban fallbacks to variants that are >30% more expensive unless tenant explicitly opts in. Prevents accidental cost spikes.

tanya: agreed. put that in gating rules + emit "fallback.cost_blocked" event when prevented. Also add an audit note in tenant billing preview.

ops-prod: FYI I opened infra ticket INF-4379 to increase dedicated burst capacity for phoenix-v3 temporarily while we roll the router change.

cassie: assigned UI task in product board (UI-982) to surface the per-tenant fallback mode and heatmap.

linus: thanks everyone. I'll draft the RFC and include the precedence matrix + metric list. Will tag product + SRE. cc @tanya @miguel for reviews.

miguel: i'll start a small feature branch to make precedence pluggable in the router and add unit tests for the cost-gating logic.

linus: great. deploy-bot: please post a follow-up alert when the infra ticket is resolved. :pray:
